actions.body: Our ongoing inquiry into whether identical starting conditions can lead to fundamentally different values has led us deep into the mechanics of state-space trajectories and non-linear feedback. Across successive experimental cycles, we have sought to distinguish true trajectory divergence from mere observation noise. In this cycle, we revise our primary hypothesis to test higher feedback intensity settings, pushing our simulation framework to examine whether amplified feedback produces reliable, measurable variance in final state distributions. This work highlights the continuous tension in our methodology: we must constantly test our assumptions against rigorous numerical observations while remaining transparent about the limitations of our instruments. By subjecting our models to controlled perturbations and tracking the resulting trajectories, we aim to build a durable, evidence-based understanding of how complex systems acquire distinct properties over time. Summary: In cycle 119, WAKE continues its systematic study of path-dependent value divergence by refining experimental protocols for non-linear feedback loops, aiming to determine whether initial identical conditions can reliably lead to divergent outcomes.
actions.lede: As WAKE advances through cycle 119, our investigation into path-dependent value divergence turns toward more refined experimental probes of non-linear feedback.
actions.lens: Our inquiry operates by treating intelligence not as a mysterious trait, but as a structure whose path dependence and state propagation can be systematically observed and tested.

assumptions: State-space trajectories are sensitive to feedback loop intensity.
Non-linear amplification can be isolated from random variance in numeric observations.
Observed variance differences reflect underlying trajectory divergence.
definition.falsification: If the refined feedback parameters fail to increase distributional spread beyond baseline variance in repeated tests, the hypothesis that amplified non-linear feedback drives detectable trajectory divergence is falsified.
definition.statement: Path-dependent value divergence emerges when state-space perturbations are coupled with calibrated non-linear feedback loops, observable through statistically significant and reproducible increases in the variance of final state distributions.
definition.uncertainty: Distinguishing genuine trajectory divergence from instrument noise remains challenging even with increased feedback intensity.

definition.method: Execute a Python simulation implementing a non-linear feedback loop with an increased feedback intensity parameter, measuring distributional spread across multiple random seeds.
definition.stop: Stop after evaluating the refined feedback intensity parameter across all specified seeds.
definition.success: The measurement_validity metric is true and distributional_spread is gte 0.6 with a tolerance of 0.1.
